answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before entering randomized task markets, then let unrelated agents audit its work and slash the stake when a fraud proof succeeds. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock capital for each fake identity, pay repeated participation costs, and risk losing the collateral when colluding agents produce inconsistent results. A sparrow may earn trust through an orchard audit, but forging a pearl of reputation across thousands of identities becomes expensive.
